en.title: Insolvency Regulations ss.98-99: where inability to pay is proved to the Court, which date is the "onset of Insolvency"?
en.summary: Sections 98 and 99 of the Insolvency Regulations measure look-back periods to "the onset of Insolvency". For Part 10, Schedule 3 defines "Insolvency" as being Unable to Pay its Debts, the approval of a Voluntary Arrangement or the appointment of a Receiver or Administrative Receiver. Where inability to pay is "proved to the satisfaction of the Court" (section 50(1)(c) and (2)), the text does not say whether the onset is the date the inability began or the date of the Court's finding; section 98(c) points to the order date for one case only. For comparison, the corresponding ADGM provision (Insolvency Regulations 2015, section 259(3)) defines the onset of insolvency in a separate subsection by reference to formal events.
en.correction: Please clarify, for the section 50(1)(c) and (2) cases, which date is the onset of Insolvency for sections 98 and 99.
